name: Whisper large-v3
notes: ENCODER-DECODER. THE ENCODER IS THE COMPUTE-HEAVY PART AND THE DECODER IS TRIVIAL, and the config makes the split explicit: is_encoder_decoder true, max_source_positions 1500, max_target_positions 448. ENCODER (the cost): 32 layers, d_model 1280, 20 heads, encoder_ffn_dim 5120, gelu, run ONCE over the full 30s log-mel spectrogram (num_mel_bins 128, 3,000 frames at the Whisper hop) compressed to 1,500 encoder positions. Attention is bidirectional and there is NO KV CACHE for it -- it is a single full-sequence forward pass, not incremental decoding, so nothing about the encoder is cached between calls. Its ~0.64B parameters are the majority of the model and all of the attention work. DECODER (the trivial part): ALSO 32 layers here -- and this is the detail most write-ups get wrong. decoder_layers is 32 in this config, NOT 4. The famous shallow 4-layer decoder belongs to whisper-large-v3-TURBO (see that record), not to large-v3. decoder_attention_heads 20, decoder_ffn_dim 5120, max_target_positions 448. KV CACHE -- TWO SEPARATE RESIDENCES, and this field covers only the first: (a) DECODER SELF-ATTENTION KV, which grows with generated tokens: 32 layers * 20 kv_heads * 64 head_dim * 2 (K and V) * 2 bytes (fp16, per torch_dtype) = 163,840 B/token = 160 KiB/token. That is the value in kv_cache_bytes_per_token. (b) DECODER CROSS-ATTENTION K/V over the 1,500 encoder frames, which is CONSTANT per request and does not grow: 32 layers * 20 heads * 64 head_dim * 1500 frames * 2 * 2 bytes = 245,760,000 B = 234 MiB per in-flight request. This is the number that actually determines concurrency for Whisper, and it is larger than a full 448-token decode's self-attention KV (448 * 163,840 = 73 MiB) by 3x. DO NOT compare Whisper's memory footprint to an autoregressive text model using per-token KV alone: one request pins 234 MiB of cross-attention KV before a single token is emitted. FLOP PROFILE: encoder-decoder ASR has a fundamentally different shape from autoregressive decode. Precompute is a dense 32-layer bidirectional pass over 1,500 positions -- O(N^2) attention in the encoder, fully compute-bound and trivially parallel across the batch. Decode is at most 448 steps of a small-batch memory-bound GEMV over 160 KiB/token. For a 30s clip the encoder is >95% of the FLOPs. A GPU that is badly utilized decoding text will be near peak utilisation running the Whisper encoder. kv_cache_bytes_per_token is set from the DECODER ONLY because the encoder has no cache at all. flops_per_token_active is left NULL rather than 2*params: for an encoder-decoder that formula describes neither the encoder's 1,500-position precompute nor the decoder's cheap decode, and recording it would be actively misleading. STREAMING vs OFFLINE: this checkpoint is an OFFLINE model. Whisper's encoder is bidirectional over the full 30s window, so you cannot stream it -- you must buffer a full 30s chunk. Streaming ASR requires either a causal/chunked encoder or overlapping-window tricks with a latency penalty. params_b 1.543 = HF API safetensors total (1,543,490,560).
